notes:
Lead: small NYC-based edtech building teacher-facing copilots for formative assessment and in-class helpers. Inbound via blog post about low-cost moderation. Primary ask: hosted API that is cheap and easy to integrate, minimal ops.

Key requirements / quotes:
- "Teachers must be able to moderate quickly — we need automated filters + human review hooks." (founder)
- Latency target: ~<500ms median for chat in the teacher panel; acceptable tail up to 1s for larger prompts.
- Cost sensitivity: budgeted ~$500-$1k/mo initially; will scale if clear cost per student decreases. Request explicit per-1k-token pricing examples and suggestions for cheap model fallbacks.
- Models: prefer a medium-sized open model; asked about Redwood-curated defaults and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants for cost reduction. Interested in embeddings for quick content search but will prioritize chat and moderation first.
- Security: SMB but schools will require SSO/SAML for teacher accounts; they asked about audit logs and basic retention controls. FERPA question surfaced — want guidance, not a blocker.
- Deployment: public cloud only (GCP us-central1 preference). No on-prem or VPC for initial phase.
- Integration: needs quickstart examples in Python and JS; asked about webhooks for moderation events and batching for saving tokens.

Timeline notes: want to run a 2-week PoC with live teacher cohort (~20 teachers). PoC goals: measure latency under load, false-positive rate on moderation (tweak thresholds), and monthly cost projection.

Internal notes / AE shorthand: try to push hosted_api free credits; prepare 2 config examples: one aggressive moderation + human-review workflow, one permissive with rate-limited human-in-the-loop. Provide sample token cost calc for 20 teachers x avg 200 messages/day.

Blockers called out on call: monthly credit cap, clarity on retention + deletion APIs, concurrent session limits. Agreed: AE to send pricing deck + security FAQ (drive links), SE to prepare PoC template.

Ask: Can Redwood provide a low-cost fallback model recommendation and an example of caching/batching config that reduces token spend by ~30%?
